title: .netrc: password token in multi-line and single-line entries
summary: A synthetic .netrc entry with machine, login and password on separate lines, and the same entry written on a single line.
rationale: The secret is a bare token after the word password with no quotes, colon or equals sign, and the same entry is valid in two layouts. A rule that needs the value on its own line, or that anchors on punctuation, misses one of the two.

expectation.rationale: Flag the token that follows the password keyword. curl's page documents both layouts, says a password token supplies the password for the login and says the file must be unreadable by other users when the token is present. The login is not given a span: the page calls it the username string and says nothing on confidentiality. The claim is scoped to curl's handling of the format.

sources.supports: Each field is provided as a sequence of letters that ends with a space or newline. ... It can also be written on a single line with the same functionality.
password string: Supply a password. ... if this token is present in the .netrc file you really should make sure the file is not readable by anyone besides the user.
